global_constraints.CRITICAL_RULE: Labels are IMMUTABLE ground truth. The algorithm must be tuned to match the labels, NEVER the other way around.
forbidden_actions: Changing startFrame, endFrame, or cameraOrientation values in labels
Adding or removing shots from labels
Adjusting labels to match algorithm output
global_constraints.failure_response: If algorithm cannot match labels within tolerance, document the gap in algorithm-learnings.md and try a different algorithmic approach. NEVER modify labels.

analysis_approach: Read poses.json around labeled start/end frames (±10 frames)
Examine ALL available pose landmarks at labeled frames vs detected frames
Identify what makes labeled frames distinct from surrounding frames
freedom_to_experiment: Try ANY pose metrics that distinguish labeled frames (not limited to wrist/knee)
Work backwards: find end frame first, then derive start frame
Work from middle: find peak/apex of shot, then expand to find boundaries
Combine multiple signals (e.g., wrist height + shoulder rotation + hip position)
Use velocity, acceleration, or rate-of-change of any landmark
Use relative positions between landmarks (e.g., wrist relative to shoulder)
Use z-depth patterns for orientation and motion phase detection
iteration_process: 1. Run test, note which shots fail and by how many frames
2. Load poses.json for failing video, examine frames around labeled boundaries
3. Hypothesize what signal would correctly identify the labeled frame
5. If regression in other videos, refine approach to work for all
algorithm_tuning_guidance.success_criteria: Algorithm detects frames within ±8 of labels using consistent logic across all videos
